We already have deep, verified context on the Zimmermann PWA project's Confluence (space key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net, root page 241434627) and Jira (project key SFCC, board id 500 "SFCC board"). A second, higher-level "Executive Readout" planning meeting just happened, covering a strategic pivot to component-driven delivery. I have detailed notes from that meeting and need you to do a FAST, TARGETED verification pass on specific claims — not a broad exploratory research pass like a prior session already did. Read-only throughout — do not modify, comment on, or transition anything.

**Already-established context — do not re-derive, just use it:**
- Jira board 500, project SFCC. Real sprints: Sprint 1 (id 497) closed 7–27 Jul 2026; Sprint 2 (id 567) active, closing 10 Aug 2026; Sprint 3 (id 568) future/starting, 11–24 Aug 2026.
- Known epics: SFCC-1 "Platform Setup & Environments", SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components" (To Do), SFCC-5 PDP, SFCC-6 PLP, SFCC-7 "Search & Recommendations", SFCC-11 Cart, SFCC-19 "Regional Storefronts".
- Known people: Tash Lay (= Natasha Lay, ACN/Accenture Delivery Lead, covers for Izzy), Isabel "Izzy" Chaloner (the other ACN Delivery Lead), Hazel Marie Cacalda (Scrum Master, both squads), Jasmijn Tsang (Lead BA).
- Our principal (who we're briefing) goes by "Angelo" in the new meeting notes — his full name is Marcel Angelo Navarro, Frontend (FED) Lead spanning both squads.
- SFCC-240 "Spike: Figma-to-React Implementation Workflow" was previously found sitting in Sprint 2 — but the new meeting notes claim it's targeted for completion "at the end of Sprint 3" instead. This is an unresolved discrepancy to chase down.
- Confluence "04.7 Component Inventory" (page id 400195591) is a live tracker mapped to the Figma design system, with columns including component Type/Name/Variants/Pages/Status/PWA-Kit-or-Contentful, listing (among others) "Product Card Base", "Product Card Group", "Product Cards with Lookbook" as Modules.
- Confluence "04.71 Writing User Stories for Components" (page id 400195600) is the new Level-1-component-epic vs Level-2-page-epic story-writing methodology doc.

**New meeting notes reference these NEW names we have not yet identified:** "Epsom" (appears to be a senior/exec figure directing the meeting, calling out action items to named individuals — e.g. "Epsom specifically called out: Tim, Victor, Gids, Angelo" for estimate scrutiny, and "Angelo, Victor, Hazel" for capacity planning), "Kiera" (identified Country Selector / Language Selector as the remaining Regional Storefront components), "Victor" and "Gids" (named alongside "Tim" and "Angelo" repeatedly for estimate validation and a future component-story-writing alignment session). "Tim" was already known from a prior session as the person behind the original informal component-based-story precedent.

Please investigate and report back on these 7 questions:

1. **Identify "Epsom", "Kiera", "Victor", and "Gids"** — try Confluence's "1.2 Team Overview" (261586947), "7.1a Tool Access Tracker" (259686402), "Meeting Cadences" (322207767), confluence_search_user, and recent Jira comment/activity authorship — the same triangulation method that previously confirmed Tash Lay and Izzy Chaloner. Report confirmed role/team for each; flag clearly anywhere you can't find a confident match rather than guessing. ("Epsom" in particular may be an unusual real surname or a nickname — don't assume it's wrong just because it looks odd.)

2. **SFCC-240 current state** — jira_get_issue on SFCC-240. What sprint is it currently assigned to (native Sprint field / board bucket), what's its status, full description, and do any comments indicate blockers or a revised completion target? Resolve whether "end of Sprint 3" (per the new meeting notes) is consistent with Jira's current state, or whether it has slipped/moved from Sprint 2.

3. **Navigation epic** — search Jira (jira_search, e.g. `project = SFCC AND text ~ "Navigation"`) for a Navigation epic or stories, now separated from Homepage per the meeting notes. Does a dedicated Navigation epic exist yet (what key), and what's its current story list/status if so? Also re-check SFCC-90 "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI" (previously found: 5 SP, In Refinement, bundling 6 content modules) — does its current description still include navigation-related content, or has it already been trimmed following the described separation?

4. **Regional Storefront — Country Selector / Language Selector** — search Jira under epic SFCC-19 "Regional Storefronts" for Country Selector / Language Selector stories. Do they exist yet, and what's their status? Also check Confluence's "04.7 Component Inventory" (400195591) for whether these two components are listed with a design-readiness status.

5. **Real Sprint 4 and Sprint 5 dates** — jira_get_sprints_from_board (board 500) — find the actual dates for Sprint 4 and Sprint 5, so we know the true "end of Sprint 5" deadline the meeting committed Regional Storefront completion to.

6. **Does the Component Inventory already solve Tim's shared-component-mapping ask?** — the meeting notes say Tim flagged that the team lacks a clear map of which components are shared/reused across multiple pages (using "Product Card" as his example), and that no owner was assigned for this work. Re-check Confluence's "04.7 Component Inventory" (400195591) specifically: does its "Pages" column actually capture cross-page reuse (i.e., does the Product Card Base / Product Card Group / Product Cards with Lookbook row list MULTIPLE consuming pages), or does it only record one owning page per component? This determines whether 04.7 already substantially answers Tim's ask or whether there's a genuine gap. Also check whether Tim (or anyone) has commented on that page recently (confluence_get_comments).

7. **Any Confluence page documenting this Executive Readout meeting itself** — search for a page titled something like "Executive Readout", "Steering", "Program Update", "Sprint 3 Planning", or similar, dated around now. If one exists, pull any additional detail (full attendee list, additional action items) not already captured in the notes summary we have.

Report back organized under these 7 numbered questions, citing concrete ticket keys / page IDs / status values / dates. Flag clearly anywhere you can't find a confident answer rather than speculating — this briefs a frontend lead ahead of near-term planning decisions, so precision matters more than completeness. Keep the report focused; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing next steps, not an end user directly.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.

Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. - figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
